newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China actively buying palm oil after price decline.
newsitem.headline: China actively buying palm oil after price decline.

text.p: China has been actively buying palm oil since the beginning of June as prices have fallen sharply, traders said on Friday.
"Chinese buyers are speculating that palm oil prices are near the bottom so they are buying," one trader said.
Cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) on Friday pegged China's June palm oil imports from Malaysia at 94,300 tonnes, compared with 43,100 tonnes in May.
Malaysian refined palm oil prices currently range between $515 to $520 a tonne against $550 in May, traders said.
"June is much better than May," another trader said.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Promotion Council said in early June China is expected to import around one million tonnes of palm oil from Malaysia in 1997, up from 873,616 tonnes in 1996.
The council attributed the stronger Chinese buying to lower prices and a cut in Chinese palm oil import duties, which was introduced earlier this year.
China reduced its import duty on refined palm oil to 12 percent from 18 percent, while the duty on crude palm oil imports is currently at nine percent.
Traders said China is expected to continue to actively buy Malaysian RBD palm oil, as long as prices remain favourable relative to competing U.S. soyoil.
Malaysian RBD palm oil is currently indicated about eight to to 10 dollars a tonne below U.S. soyoil, they added.
Chinese authorities have forecast that China's domestic soybean output would rise this year as the planted area has increased by 8.8 percent over 1996 to 8.1 million hectares.
